2. Relevant facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule Nisi, in brief, are that petitioner company purchased a total of 5 acres of land in the year 1951 in which the disputed land measuring 0.018 acres was mentioned as Schedule-B to the writ petition. The alleged property belonged to Bhuban Mohan Mukhopadhay Mukherjee and Srimati Nani Bala Devi which was recorded in the name of Bhuban Mohan under PS Khatian. Thereafter, it was recorded in the name of MM Ispahani, under the BS Khatian, being owner the petitioner company sold many portions thereof. The petitioner company constructed a two-storied building on a part of the said land and office bearers of the petitioner company lived therein. However, the petitioner company was in exclusive possession of the disputed 0.018 acres of land till the Liberation in 1971 and after the Liberation War, the said building was taken over by the Government authorities evicting the company's occupants. But the rest of the land has been under the possession of the petitioner company. After the independence, the petitioner company by several applications requested the authorities to release the property, but the authority did not take any effective steps to release the same. Subsequently, the said property was included in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned buildings published on 23-9-1986 and, therefore, the petitioner company preferred a case before the learned Court of Settlement under section 7(1) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 praying for the release of the said property in question. Thereafter, the said case was numbered as Case No. 336 of 1992, which was tried by the 2nd Court of Settlement, Dhaka. Afterward, on contest learned Court of Settlement by its judgment and order rejected the same. 

 7. He submits that the learned Court took the decision based on the title of the concerned property mentioning that Nani Bala Devi executed the said deed of sale along with her husband Bhuban Mohan but the name of Nani Bala was not included in the PS Khatian. He argued that the Court below wrongly took such an issue and decided the matter. According to him, Settlement Court had no authority to consider such issues for deciding a case of abandoned property which is absolutely beyond the jurisdiction.
